Subject: Request — per-1M token rates (input/output) + model list

Hi Stephanie,

We are evaluating hosted inference options for a set of internal summarization and classification workloads. Procurement asked for a simple baseline: what are your standard per-1M token rates (input vs output) and which model families do you offer via the hosted API (and any notable variants / latency tiers)? We primarily care about: 1) a strong LLM for long-form summarization, 2) a low-cost fast model for embeddings/classification, and 3) an option that supports streaming and function calling.

Also helpful: any guidance on discounts for a 1.5M tokens/month starting commit (12 months) and whether there are recommended plans (hosted vs dedicated) at that scale. We've attached a short spreadsheet with our estimated token mix.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Li
Head of AI, NovaHealth

Hi Emma — great to hear from you and thanks for the spreadsheet. Quick answers up front, then a short table below. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through specifics.

Baseline hosted API (list price, per 1M tokens):
- Input tokens: $0.40 / 1M tokens
- Output tokens: $1.20 / 1M tokens

Model inventory (hosted API, examples and tiers):
- Redwood-Large (production-quality, best for long-form summarization; supports streaming & function calling)
- Redwood-Medium (balanced cost/latency, good for instruction-following)
- Redwood-Fast (low-cost, optimized for short completions / classification)
- Embedding-Base (dense embeddings; low latency)

Notes: listed prices are baseline for hosted with no committed discount. For 1.5M tokens/month a 10–15% volume discount is typical depending on token mix and whether you prepay or commit annual spend. Dedicated (reserved capacity) typically becomes cost-effective for sustained traffic > ~10M tokens/month or when you need guaranteed throughput / isolation.

I attached our standard ratecard and I've CC'd Aditya (SE) to flag any technical constraints from your token mix.

Next step: would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday 15th or Friday 16th?

Raj — great questions, answered inline below. Looping in Aditya (SE) for any tokenization/latency specifics and Jonas (VP Sales) to confirm discount levers.

1) Input vs output: pricing is based on tokens consumed by the model call. There is no additional per-request surcharge for the hosted API aside from the token-based billing. Example: a request with 200 input tokens and 800 output tokens is billed at 200 input + 800 output according to the rates above.

2) Streaming: no separate price for streaming vs non-streaming for token charges — streaming is charged on the same per-token basis. We do not apply an extra streaming fee on hosted.

3) Embeddings: billed per 1M embeddings when using the embeddings endpoint (we include a separate embeddings SKU). If you prefer, we can convert your embeddings estimate to token-equivalent to compare — but standard practice is embeddings per-vector.

Aditya — can you confirm any notes about latency targets for Redwood-Large on 2k context summarization? The spreadsheet suggests 2k average summaries and occasional 8k bursts.

Best,
Stephanie

Hi all — quick technical read on the token mix provided: 1) For 2k average summaries the Redwood-Large profile will typically run at ~80–120ms/token p50 on our hosted fleet (region dependent). KV-cache and prefix caching help for repeated prefixes; for 8k bursts p99 will increase and you may want to consider either smaller batch sizes or a dedicated capacity if latency p99 is a strict SLA.

2) Embeddings: Embedding-Base is optimized for throughput — expect sub-10ms per vector on batch sizes of 64+. Pricing for embeddings is invoiced per 1M vectors.

3) Tokenization: we use a BPE variant; the spreadsheet's token estimates look reasonable but we'll validate on a sample prompt set during the trial.

If NovaHealth is planning a 12-month committed purchase at 1.5M tokens/month, the commercial team typically offers a tiered discount model: 10% for annual commit prepay, 12–15% if you add a usage buffer or agree to a 2x uplift review at mid-term. Jonas, please confirm if we can offer an initial 12% with a standard enterprise SOW.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
